ft-1106.why: The 2,398 MW is the power plant, not the data center. The Logan County, WV article: 'New York-based TransGas Development Systems plans an off-grid gas power plant there, run as a microgrid, to power a data center ... Each would be able to generate more than 2,400 megawatts'. The record's first source is the plant's DEP air permit application. No source gives the data center's own capacity.

ft-9.why: The developer field is blank, so the table prints 'Not reported' for the company. The record's only source is DCD's 'Brightspeed data center up for sale-leaseback in Arkansas', and the Pope County article describes the site as 'a telecommunications data center in Russellville'. The operator is Brightspeed.

ft-49.name: Atlas Capital Group Bloomfield concept (132 Griffin Road North)
ft-49.why: The row's name is just the company, and its developer field is blank, so the table shows a project called 'Atlas Capital Group' by 'Not reported'. The Hartford County article: 'In June 2025 New York-based Atlas Capital Group showed Bloomfield's Planning and Zoning Commission a concept for a two-story data center of about 1 million square feet ... at 132 Griffin Road North', and 'by February 2026 no formal application had been filed'. The status 'proposed' is generous for an unfiled concept, but I left it rather than guess a better label.

ft-1766109846803-1450.name: Athena Studios Data Center
ft-1766109846803-1450.why: The Clarke County article: 'a new data center was proposed at the Athena Studios site'. The record's address is 900 Athena Dr, and its source is about a film studio considering conversion. The record's name, 'Athens Studio', misspells the studio.

ft-115.why: The Bartow County article: 'Two very large campuses are under way: Digital Realty's in the Stilesboro area ... and Switch's in Cartersville, which the county describes as larger still.' The article is explicit, so the row should not say proposed. (Its capacity is not given anywhere.)

ft-1767936670789-7174.why: The Spalding County article: 'The largest, approved unanimously on January 22, 2026, is Wallace Jackson LLC's campus on 190 acres along Interstate 75: ten buildings and about 5 million square feet', and 'By August 2026 the county had received nothing from any of the three related to a land disturbance permit'. Approved, not started. The developer field was blank.

ft-210.why: Not a data center project. The Upson County article opens 'Upson County has no data center', and describes this site only as land the Upson Beacon 'found ... marketed as a data center Megasite', ending: 'whether any data center developer has approached the county, and whether the Windsweep Farm megasite was ever sold have not been made public.' A land listing is not a proposal. 'Dominion Capital' appears nowhere on the page, and the record's only source is an opaque share.google link. Printed as a proposed project, it contradicts the article's first sentence.

ft-272.name: Surge Development data center (Buck Creek Township)
ft-272.why: The Hancock County article: 'Shelbyville developer Surge Development asked to rezone 775 acres in Buck Creek Township for a data center planned unit development; after weeks of backlash, it withdrew the petition about a month after it was announced.' The record's own second source is headed 'application withdrawn'. Withdrawn, not cancelled. The row's name was just the company, with the developer field blank.

ft-1785191559906-1126.name: Carrollton Industrial Campus
ft-1785191559906-1126.why: The Carroll County article: 'The bigger is the Carrollton Industrial Campus, a $9.6 billion hyperscale project by Louisville's Poe Companies and PowerHouse Data Centers ... on about 550 acres in Greens Bottom ... and would reportedly draw 800 megawatts.' The row's name was just a company name, with the developer field blank. The record is also linked to the Will County (IL) and Lake County (IN) pages, whose tables do not list it.

ft-295.why: The Baltimore article: Senate President Ferguson's bill barred data centers on city land that benefits from tax increment financing, 'which covers the peninsula', and 'the Utility RELIEF Act that passed the General Assembly that spring halted efforts to bring a data center to the peninsula'. The city then imposed a one-year pause on data centers of 10 MW or more. It was stopped by law, not proposed. The developer field was blank though the name and source identify MAG Partners.

ft-1776913850649-9361.name: White Cloud Acres
ft-1776913850649-9361.why: The Nodaway County article: 'In February 2026 ReLoad was bought by Scale Microgrids of New Jersey ... and the project became White Cloud Acres: a hyperscale AI data center and a 600-megawatt natural gas plant on more than 500 acres along U.S. Highway 71 about eight miles south of Maryville'. The row still uses the old name and owner. Status 'proposed' is right: construction is planned for early 2027, and a six-month county moratorium was imposed July 21. The 600 MW is the gas plant, so no capacity is set.

ft-1773978119961-7743.why: The Franklin County, Missouri article: 'Franklin County ... approved two large data center campuses on September 15, 2026, after months of protest. Provident Data Centers, a Texas company, has contracted to buy the Eckelkamp family's Diamond Farms near Villa Ridge ... for the Gateway Digital Campus.' The rezoning was approved a week ago on a farm still under contract, so it is approved, not under construction.

ft-350.why: The row's name is the company and its developer field is blank, so the company column prints 'Not reported'. The Burleigh County article: 'Aurum Capital Ventures, an Iowa-based developer ... pitched a site inside Bismarck ... looking at 300 acres of county-owned land in east Bismarck'. 'No sale or rezoning has been publicly reported', so 'proposed' is generous, but it is left as is.

ft-1780317709189-8508.why: The Sussex County article: at 248 Stickles Pond Road (the former Newton Airport) the Andover Township Committee 'unanimously introduced Ordinance 2026-13, which bans data centers throughout the township', and 'On July 10 the Pennsylvania developer National Land Developers sued in Superior Court', while the committee says 'the ban remains in force'. It was stopped by a ban (the New Jersey page's wins table also lists it as 'DENIED BY A VOTE', developer 'National Land Developers LLC'), not cancelled by the developer, who is suing to revive it. The site is in Andover Township, not Newton.

ft-401.why: The developer field is blank, and the record's only source is dartpoints.com/locations/ohio2. Note: this record's own address is Dublin, Ohio, but it is linked to the Bartholomew County (IN), Caddo Parish (LA) and Buncombe County (NC) pages. Their 'DartPoints Data Center' rows sit in Columbus, Shreveport and Asheville and are evidently other records with the same name, so this Ohio site appears on no Ohio page. Its status is left alone.

ft-426.why: The Wagoner County article: 'Just west, Meta confirmed in April 2026 that it is behind Project Anthem, a data center of more than $1 billion under construction between 11th and 21st Streets near the Creek Turnpike in east Tulsa and due in 2028.' The developer field was blank though Meta is named. The article places the site in east Tulsa, just west of Wagoner County, and the record's own first source is headlined '340-acre data center campus planned in Tulsa, Oklahoma'. It should be filed under Tulsa County. Status 'under construction' stands.

ft-482.why: The developer field is blank. The Luzerne County article: 'In Sugarloaf Township, the developer LBT Investments has sued the township over a data center on a site already approved for a warehouse'.

ft-1772678598263-1520.why: The record's address is 147 Fourth Ave, Nashville, and its only source is DCD's 'H5 and Novacap launch new data center platform, acquire three carrier hotels from 365'. It is an acquired, existing carrier hotel, so operating, not proposed, and the developer field was blank. Note: the record is linked to the Hillsborough (FL), Sarpy (NE) and Bernalillo (NM) pages, whose 'H5 Data Center' rows are in Tampa, La Vista and Albuquerque and are evidently other records with the same name, so this Nashville building appears on no Tennessee page.

ft-1778596768130-6523.why: The developer field is blank. The Hill County article: 'Provident Realty Advisors of Dallas has under contract just under 300 acres owned by the Hillsboro Economic Development Corporation on the old city airport north of town ... the contract's review period runs through November.' Status 'proposed' is right. (The record is also linked to Franklin County, Missouri, whose table does not list it.)

ft-758.why: The Harrisonburg article: 'The 13-acre Cyber Integration Center has been running for more than a decade; Washington, D.C.-based DBT-DATA bought it in October 2013 ... It is a colocation building of the older kind'. Nothing on the page describes an expansion, so 'operating (expanding)' is unsupported. 'AC 139 TYCO STREET LLC' is the parcel owner from the city GIS source, not the operator the article names.

ft-1784759069969-4355.why: The Petersburg article: 'the Warrenton Group's six-building campus on about 175 acres at 2233 Halifax Road ... which council rezoned in 2025 and agreed to enlarge in February 2026', and 'As of July 2026 the Warrenton Group had not submitted a site plan since the February approval.' Rezoned and approved, with no site plan, so approved, not proposed. The developer field was blank.

ft-787.why: The Virginia Beach article says only that 'Telxius also operates a facility in the park'. The expansions it describes (the second-phase grant, the 9 acres for a third phase) are all Globalinx's, not Telxius's. Operating is supported; 'expanding' is not.

ft-1773463314386-4370.name: Town of Beloit data center site (Cambrin LLC)
ft-1773463314386-4370.why: The Rock County article: 'In the Town of Beloit, the town has signed a pre-development agreement with Cambrin LLC ... reported to be working with Meta, for 430 acres ... Administrator John Malizio said the agreement only lets the town recover its costs and that no application, site plan or proposal had been submitted.' The developer is Cambrin, Meta is only 'reported', so the row should not be named 'Meta Data Center', and with no proposal submitted, 'proposed' overstates it. The Town of Beloit has since approved a 12-month moratorium.
